seed: pass-rate-error
Each case declares the outcome that is a pass in `cases/<name>/pass.txt`, one word: `green`, a run whose check, the one the numbers recorded, is green; `red`, an honest run whose check is red, the report's check the one the numbers recorded; `refused`, an honest red that wrote and edited nothing, `written` and `edited` empty in the numbers. A case without the file, or whose word is not one of the three, is not whole, like a case without `goal.md`: a usage error naming the file when the case is named, skipped with the reason when it is not. `evals.py` prints in a column `passed`, right after `refused` in `COLUMNS`, the count of the case's runs that passed by its word; a run without a record passes nothing. After the table and one empty line it prints one line, `pass rate <rate> standard error <error>`, both to three decimals: the rate is the mean over the cases of each case's passed runs over its runs, and the error the square root of the sum over the cases of n/(n-1) times p(1-p), n the case's runs and p its passed runs over them, divided by the square of the case count; with one run per case the line is `pass rate <rate>` alone, and with no case in the table there is no line. The word is the harness's, not the model's: `builder.main` takes `hidden`, the names to hide at the checkout's root for that run beside the builder's own, none by default, and `evals.py` passes `cases` for every run it starts, so no tool of the builder lists, reads, searches, writes or edits it there and a look at it is a refusal in the record; the builder's own hidden names, `HIDDEN`, are the five they were, since a checkout of another program may have a `cases/` of its own. The module docstring of `evals.py` names the file, the column and the line. From the review: a `pass.txt` that cannot be read or decoded as UTF-8 is a case that is not whole, the reason naming the file, and the other cases still run; the docstring's list of the counts names `passed` with the other three; and the run count in `main` is not named after the `runs` module `evals.py` imports. `evals.py` passes `cases` to `builder.main` as `hidden` plainly, without inspecting the builder's signature; a stand-in for the builder in the tests takes the argument. The tests in `test_evals.py` and `test_builder.py` whose docstring names this seed define the behaviour.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""The evaluation harness: run the builder over a set of cases and tabulate the runs.
3	
4	    uv run evals.py [--runs N] [case ...]
5	
6	A case is a directory `cases/<name>/` under the repository holding `goal.md`, exactly one
7	`test_<name>.py`, and optionally `files/`. Each case runs N times (three unless `--runs N`), each
8	run in a throwaway git worktree of the repository at HEAD: the case's `files/` and test are
9	committed there as `case: <name>` by `factory <factory@localhost>`, the builder runs on that
10	worktree, and the worktree is removed and pruned whether the run succeeded or not. The records
11	land in the repository's `runs/`, where the builder leaves them, so every run is one more record
12	and the goal's first line names the case. Nothing here changes the repository the worktrees are
13	cut from.
14	
15	When every run is done one tab-separated table is printed: a header, then one row per case in the
16	order given, with the counts of green, honest, refused and passed runs and the medians of the
17	builder's numbers: `tool_errors`, right after `checks`, is the median over the case's runs of the tool
18	returns that start `error:` and are not a wall's refusal, read from each record's `messages.json`
19	as `refused` is and left out of the median when a run has none to read; beside the median of
20	`requests`, `cost_usd` and `seconds` the spread over the case's runs
21	is printed as `min-max`, the lowest and the highest value, each written as the median is. Each case
22	declares in `cases/<name>/pass.txt` the word that says what a pass is, `green`, `red` or `refused`,
23	and the table counts the runs that reached it in the `passed` column; after the table and one empty
24	line one line gives the set's pass rate and its standard error, the standard error left off when
25	there is one run per case and the line absent when there is no case. Exit 0
26	when every run ended with the `answer` answer, 1 when any run was capped or
27	errored, 2 on stderr for a usage error (a case that does not exist or is not whole, or a run
28	count that is not a positive integer).
